name: Tian (Gao Tianliang)
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2019 League of Legends World Championship with FunPlus Phoenix and was named Finals MVP at age 19, also winning LPL Summer 2019.
early_history_summary: Gao Tianliang was born in Yanbian, Jilin Province, and moved to Weihai, Shandong at age two. His father introduced him to gaming through Red Alert, and Tian reached Diamond on the Chinese Super Server at age 13. He turned pro at 15 with YM Esports, joined Suning in 2018, then FPX in December 2018 where he formed a dominant jungle-mid duo with Doinb.
family_context_summary: Born to a family of traditional Chinese medicine practitioners in Yanbian; father was relatively open-minded and introduced Tian to gaming, eventually supporting his pro career despite initial family resistance.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a gamer who introduced Tian to video games via Red Alert; family lineage was in traditional Chinese medicine, not esports or gaming industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YM Esports pipeline, Doinb partnership, LPL ecosystem, early solo queue ranking, family gaming exposure
evidence_summary: Tian reached Diamond on the Chinese Super Server at 13 and turned pro at 15 through the YM Esports pipeline, known as the 'West Point' of the LPL. His father introduced him to gaming and eventually supported his pro career despite the family's traditional Chinese medicine background. At FPX, he formed a dominant jungle-mid partnership with Doinb that led to winning the 2019 World Championship and Finals MVP at age 19. The LPL ecosystem and YM developmental pipeline were key accelerators in his trajectory.
starting_point: Born in Yanbian, Jilin Province to a traditional Chinese medicine family; father was a gamer who introduced him to video games; family moved to Weihai, Shandong when he was two.

He won his first LPL MVP in 2017 with QG/JD Gaming, then joined FPX in December 2018 where his unique playstyle and partnership with jungler Tian led to the 2019 World Championship.

evidence_summary: Doinb was a high-elo solo queue streamer in Korea, praised by Faker, who moved to China at 18 to join Qiao Gu Reapers in the developmental league. His father supported the move, which came during the 2014-15 Korean exodus to the LPL. Despite not speaking Mandarin and never having lived away from parents, Doinb quickly excelled, reaching the LPL finals in his first year. His unique champion pool and playstyle, combined with his jungle partnership with Tian at FPX, led to winning the 2019 World Championship and his second LPL MVP at age 22.

name: MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson)
milestone_by_age_26: Reached 100,000 YouTube subscribers in August 2016 at age 18, then 1 million subscribers in May 2017 at age 19, and 10 million subscribers by November 2018 at age 20, becoming the most-subscribed YouTuber on the platform.
early_history_summary: James Stephen Donaldson was born in Wichita, Kansas, and raised in Greenville, North Carolina, by parents who served in the military. He uploaded his first YouTube video in February 2012 at age 13 under the channel name MrBeast6000. After years of experimenting with content types, his 'Worst Intros' series helped him reach 30K subscribers by 2016. His 'I Counted to 100,000!' video in January 2017 went viral, catapulting him to 1M subscribers by May 2017 and 10M by November 2018. He dropped out of college after two weeks to pursue YouTube full-time.
family_context_summary: Born to U.S. military veteran parents in Wichita, Kansas; parents divorced in 2007; mother Susan raised him and his older brother CJ as a single parent; diagnosed with Crohn's disease as a teenager; middle-class upbringing in Greenville, North Carolina.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were U.S. military veterans with no background in media, entertainment, or content creation; father Charles Donaldson; mother Susan Parisher.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YouTube algorithm obsession, early start at 13, self-reinvestment, creator economy wave, Crohn's disease constraint, friend team
evidence_summary: MrBeast started his YouTube channel at 13 in 2012 with no equipment, no industry connections, and middle-class parents who were military veterans. He spent four years obsessively studying the YouTube algorithm and experimenting with content before his 'I Counted to 100,000!' video went viral in January 2017. He reinvested every dollar earned back into his channel, brought in childhood friends as team members, and rode the YouTube creator economy wave to become the most-subscribed YouTuber ever. His Crohn's disease diagnosis led him to quit sports, intensifying his focus on YouTube. He dropped out of college after two weeks, and his mother kicked him out, creating urgency that fueled his dedication.

name: Ryan Trahan
milestone_by_age_26: Crossed 100,000 YouTube subscribers around 2018 at age 19-20 and launched the viral 'penny series' in 2017, growing to 2.31M subscribers by early 2020 and 23.5M subscribers by 2026.
early_history_summary: Ryan Michael Trahan was born in Sugar Land, Texas, and attended Rice High School where he graduated as valedictorian in 2017. He started his YouTube channel in October 2013 at age 15, initially producing running content. He co-founded Neptune Bottle water brand in 2016 with friend Caden Wiese while attending Texas A&M University as a cross country runner. The NCAA ruled him ineligible for using his YouTube channel while being a student athlete, forcing him to choose between college athletics and YouTube; he dropped out and moved to Florida to pursue content creation full-time.
